approaches.name: GIS-enabled SUTEM irrigation MIS rollout for water user associations
approaches.description: The project scales a GIS-enabled irrigation management information system to 378 water user associations, with tablets, hardware, training and registry links for water and land decisions. Practices: SUTEM irrigation information system for WUA water management; Web-based GIS-enabled participatory water monitoring system for WUAs; GIS-enabled SUTEM MIS for national WUA performance monitoring; Nationwide SUTEM MIS rollout after field trials; SUTEM irrigation MIS mainstreamed across 378 Water User Associations; SUTEM irrigation MIS mainstreamed in 378 WUAs; GIS-enabled SUTEM irrigation MIS integrated with land and civil registries; SUTEM irrigation management software for water user associations; Tablet-based GIS field data collection for SUTEM rollout.
approaches.why_innovative: New service: web-based irrigation MIS for WUA operations - cue: 'pilots' | category Technological; adoption apply; judged in 1 round(s); final check: digital core, in_use before 2019

evidence.text: Beneficiaries also include approximately 100 staff from DSI’s regional offices and 600 staff from 378 WUAs, who will be equipped and trained in the use of the SUTEM irrigation information system, which will strengthen WUA’s capacity for O&M, water conservation, financial management, governance, M&E, and communications.

extra_evidence.text: The project will be monitored through DSI’s existing Management Information System (MIS), which will be further enhanced by the implementation of the national, web-based and GIS-enabled participatory water monitoring system for the WUAs (Subcomponent 2A).

Component 2: Innovation and Institutional Support (US$2 million): This component will provide direct design and implementation support to DSI in the following areas: (a) Subcomponent 2 (A) -Designing and Piloting a National Program for WUA Capacity-Building (GEF, US$1.29 million): This GEF funded activity will provide support to DSI for the mainstreaming, at the national level, of their newly developed irrigation Management Information System (MIS), called SUTEM[1].

The MIS, which is GIS enabled, is designed to support smart-decision making and increase the WUAs operational efficiency by centralizing data related to physical (irrigation network condition, type of water source and availability, etc.), socio-economic (total number of water users/farmers, crop types and cropping patterns, etc.) and managerial (assessment and collection of service charges, investment needs, etc) aspects of the targeted irrigation schemes.
In an initial phase the system will be implemented across 378 WUAs covering a total irrigation area of 3.08 million ha in the country.
Under Component 2, DSI’s Department of Operations and Maintenance will implement the GEF- funded roll-out of the nation-wide SUTEM system (Component 2A).
This Department has previously developed the SUTEM MIS software, and is currently completing the field-trials of the system.

Sub-component 2.1 and 2.2 of the Turkey Irrigation Modernization Project will be supported with GEF-6 funding and will promote sustainable agricultural land management practices to reduce the drivers of land degradation in Turkey by (i) mainstreaming at the national level an irrigation Management Information System (MIS), called SUTEM, in all of its 378 Water User Associations (WUA) covering an irrigated area of 3.08 million ha, encouraging evidence-based multi-stakeholder decision making for better land and water management, and (ii) piloting a sustainable energy and groundwater irrigation management system in Bolvadin, Afyon, with the potential of scaling up in other regions of Turkey, to demonstrate how such approaches can simultaneously reduce both groundwater pumping and electricity costs of irrigation in overexploited aquifers, thereby liberating resources for investments that increase agricultural productivity.

In this context, MoFWA has allocated US$2 million from the Land Degradation Focal Area for the implementation of two initiatives that will help reduce the drivers of land degradation and promote sustainable land and water management: (i) the mainstreaming at the national level of an irrigation Management Information System (MIS), called SUTEM, in 378 Water User Associations (WUA), and (ii) the piloting of a sustainable energy and groundwater irrigation system in Bolvadin, Afyon.

Better availability and management of agricultural land and irrigation information via the SUTEM software will allow for more efficient and effective decision making towards sustainable land and water management.
This GEF funded activity will provide support to DSI for the mainstreaming, at the national level, of their newly developed irrigation Management Information System (MIS), called SUTEM.

The SUTEM, which is GIS enabled, is designed to support smart decision making for improved land and water management and increase the WUAs operational efficiency by centralizing data related to physical (irrigation network condition, type of water source and availability, etc), socio-economic (total number of water users/farmers, crop types and cropping patterns, etc.) and managerial (assessment and collection of service charges, investment needs, etc.) aspects of the targeted irrigation schemes.

Having in view the importance of multi-stakeholder planning and investments for sustainable land management investments, the SUTEM benefits and is well-integrated with relevant existing information systems from related agencies such as the Directorate General of Civil Registration and Citizenship Affairs, the Directorate General of Land Registry and Cadastre and the Directorate General of Agricultural Reform.
Facility and Inventory Gathering and management of geographic/location enabled information of irrigation facilities and network data in a single platform 3.
Assessment and Collection Assessment and collection of operation and maintenance fee/service charge for water use.

Irrigation Management Collection of declarations of water subscribers, determining the amount of water to be used within the irrigation season on an acquiring organization basis and signing a protocol, preparation of general irrigation planning and planned water distribution programs, determination of the actual amount of water use, evaluation of the implementation reports.

In addition, each WUA will be provided with a tablet (iPad) given its ease for mobility to exploit to the fullest the location specific/GIS characteristics of the SUTEM for on-site data collection, in this way increasing data collection quality.
DSI will utilize GEF funds for the acquisition of the hardware (desktop computer, laptop and tablets) needed for the SUTEM roll out in 378 WUAs, covering 3.08 million ha of irrigated land.
